topic: Weak and Strong Symbols in Linker Symbol Resolution
explanation: Weak and strong symbols are fundamental linker concepts that determine how multiply-defined symbols are resolved during the linking stage. Strong symbols represent definitive, authoritative symbol definitions—by default, all symbols are strong, meaning if the linker encounters two strong definitions with the same name, it raises a multiple definition error. Functions and initialized global variables automatically get strong symbols. Weak symbols, on the other hand, provide a flexible mechanism that allows multiple definitions of the same symbol name without causing linker errors. When both a strong and weak symbol exist with the same name, the strong symbol always takes precedence. Uninitialized global variables (BSS section) automatically get weak symbols. In C/C++, weak symbols can be explicitly created using `__attribute__((weak))` in GCC/Clang or the `#pragma weak` preprocessor directive. This mechanism is crucial for creating overridable default implementations in libraries and frameworks, allowing developers to replace default behavior without modifying library code. The linker's symbol resolution follows these rules: strong beats weak, multiple strong symbols cause errors, multiple weak symbols result in arbitrary selection of one copy.
keywords: weak strong symbols, linker symbol resolution, multiple definition error, weak attribute
